# dsh-acp-server
**Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server for the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).**
Drive a full dsh coding agent - streaming output, tool calls, permission prompts, durable sessions -
from Zed or any ACP v1 client, exactly like opencode or Gemini CLI.
English | 中文
## What it does
A `dsh` profile bundle that boots the entire DeepSeek Harness (agent loop, tools, sandbox, session p
ersistence) with an ACP v1 JSON-RPC server instead of - or alongside - the web UI.
| ACP method | Status |
| `initialize` | ✅ full capability advertisement (`loadSession`, `promptCapabilities.image`, `sessio

nCapabilities.list/resume/close/delete`) |
| `authenticate` | ✅ no-op success (dsh credentials live

outside ACP; empty `authMethods`) |
| `session/new` | ✅ durable dsh agent + modes + slash-command ad

vertisement + initial `configOptions` |
| `session/prompt` | ✅ streaming `agent_message_chunk` / `ag
ent_thought_chunk` (reasoning), `plan` updates, full tool-call lifecycle, `{stopReason, usage}`; fai
led turns reject with a JSON-RPC error carrying the cause; **image blocks** persist through the dsh

attachments service; a single `/command` text block routes to the dsh command registry |
| `session/
set_config_option` | ✅ per-session `model` (`<provider>/<model>`) and `reasoning_effort` overrides;
live effect on the next step; unsupported knobs/values refuse with precise `-32602`; `config_option_

update` pushed on change |
| `usage_update` / `usage` | ✅ context usage (`used`/`size`) pushed from

token accounting; the prompt response sums the turn's tokens (experimental ACP field) |
| `session/l

ist` | ✅ every persisted + live session (id, cwd, title) |
| `session/resume` | ✅ reopen a persisted

session without replay (standard form of the vendor method) |
| `session/load` | ✅ reopen + replay

the transcript as `user_message_chunk` / `agent_message_chunk` |
| `session/set_mode` | ✅ `default`

⇄ `plan`, bridged to dsh plan mode, with `current_mode_update` push |
| `available_commands_update`

| ✅ the dsh command registry, advertised per session and refreshed each turn |
| `session/request_pe

rmission` | ✅ dsh's approval seam bridged to the client (allow once/always, reject once/always) |
|
`elicitation/create` | ✅ form-mode dsh user questions for clients declaring `elicitation.form`; one
single-select question falls back to permission buttons; richer questions fall through to the host's

answerer |
[该节后续省略]
## The two final forms
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Form 1 — standalone (`dsh-acp-server`)
After `npm i -g dsh-acp-server` (or via `npx`). The bin boots `dsh --profile acp` with the current s
tdio and passes every launcher flag through (`serve --port 7800`, `--patch extra.yml`). First use in
a DSH home auto-bootstraps the `acp` profile with the official `dsh plugin` command - bootstrap out
put goes to stderr, so an editor's stdout only ever sees ACP frames.
Zed → Settings → `agent_servers` (full sample in examples/zed-settings.json):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Form 2 — together (`dsh web`)
Install into the `web` profile once; every plain `dsh web` boot then serves the GUI and ACP on one p
all into the `web` profile once; every plain `dsh web` boot then serves the GUI and ACP on one port:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Prefer to keep `web` untouched? `node bin/setup-webacp.mjs --clone webacp` gives the same on `dsh --
web` untouched? `node bin/setup-webacp.mjs --clone webacp` gives the same on `dsh --profile webacp`.
The script writes a row-level `inject: [agents, agentDefaultModel, webServer]` so Cordis starts the
acp-server fiber only after the shared `webServer` service exists - the stdio transport can never ra
ce a web boot. A hand install without that row is safe too: the plugin web-mounts late via service p
rovisioning (terminal boots skip stdio entirely; daemon boots get an EOF grace window). The full row
is documented in examples/patches/web-mounted.yml.
Why a bin instead of the literal `dsh acp-server`: the dsh launcher hardcodes its app subcommands (`
web`, `plugin`) and parses argv before any plugin loads, so a bundle cannot register one; the wrappe
r is the same single-command shape.
## Drive dsh from a script (`run`)
`dsh-acp-server run` is a one-shot CLI for **external agents and orchestrators**: it spawns the real
`dsh --profile acp`, speaks ACP to it through the same SDK every other client uses, prints the answ
er, and exits. No ACP client implementation required:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Default output** is the final assistant answer as plain text on stdout; progress (tool calls, pe
rmission notes) goes to stderr. `--json` prints exactly one object: `{sessionId, stopReason, text, t

oolCalls: [{title, status}], usage?, error?}`.
- **Exit codes**: `0` done · `1` error · `2` timeout
(the turn was cancelled) · `3` cancelled · `4` a permission request was denied. A script branches on

the code, never on parsing prose.
- `--session <id>` resumes a persisted session (`dsh-acp-server r
un ... --session "$(cat last-session)"` keeps one conversation across invocations); without it each

run creates a fresh session.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
Transport choice is deterministic at mount: `serve` subcommand → standalone HTTP server; a `webServe
r` service present (or arriving late) → routes registered on the shared server; otherwise stdio.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Source layout: `src/connection.ts` (method handlers) · `translate.ts` / `config-options.ts` (pure wi
re mappings, unit-tested) · `event-bridge.ts` / `perm-bridge.ts` (dsh ⇄ ACP seams) · `session-delete
.ts` (guarded persisted-session cleanup) · `cli/run.ts` (the one-shot CLI; `cli/run-core.ts` is its
pure mapping layer) · `http-transport.ts` (shared HTTP router) · `serve-startup.ts` (the `serve` sub
command) · `config.ts` (schema) · `table.ts` (session registry).
Full research behind every mapping: `research/` - ACP protocol, DSH architecture, prior art, design
